# STRATOS: Bridging the Symbolic-to-Numeric Gap in Spatio-Temporal Text-to-SQL for Meteorological Data

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#stratos)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-14**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.03501v2) · arXiv:2607.03501v2, revised 11 November 2026. PDF header matches this version; the PDF has 13 pages although the abstract-page comments say 12 pages.

**Reading coverage:** All 13 PDF pages: abstract, Sections I-VII, acknowledgments and references; all five figures and eight tables. Figures 1-5 and dense evaluation/error tables were also inspected visually. No appendices are present.

## Research question

Meteorological SQL requires resolving place names, units and climate-event definitions absent from table schemas. A fast query may still answer the wrong geographic or temporal interpretation.

## Method

An LLM chooses Wikidata location candidates, retrieves OpenStreetMap geometry, and injects ontology definitions plus array-schema hints. A PostgreSQL-specific rewriter converts large coordinate IN-lists into VALUES subqueries, alongside expression indexes. Geospatial grounding and SQL rewriting are separate stages.

## Evaluation

From 161 expert-checked seeds, the workload generates 7,520 NL/SQL pairs: 3,760 request instances with exact and approximate spatial variants. DAIL-SQL and OpenSearch-SQL with two model backbones are evaluated on 1,504 pairs from four held-out locations using result equality, efficiency, ablations and error analysis.

## What the results support

The reported grounding gains coexist with substantial structural and domain errors. Error analysis explicitly recognizes valid aggregation alternatives that fail the single gold result. Rewriting improves PostgreSQL latency; bounding-box approximation trades speed for answers that can differ materially.

## Limits and qualifications

There is no evaluated user-clarification, abstention or interpretation-coverage policy. Exact and approximate targets are deliberately different, not equivalent rewrites. EXPLAIN establishes planning viability rather than semantic correctness. Runtime means exclude designated nonfinishing pairs; the zero-timeout gold-query experiment differs from generated-query evaluation. Workload release and independent reproduction were not verified.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Useful adjacent evidence for domain-knowledge grounding and evaluation under underspecification, especially when a benchmark rejects a reasonable answer or an efficiency shortcut changes the requested region.
